question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $△ABC$ is an isosceles triangle. Consequently, the base angles must have equal measure:

$$
m∠A=m∠ABC={72}^{∘}
$$

Also, since $△CDB$ is an isosceles triangle, we have:

$$
m∠D=m∠BCD
$$

Since $∠ABC$ and $∠CBD$ are supplementary, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠ABC+m∠CBD & ={180}^{∘} \\ {72}^{∘}+m∠CBD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠CBD & ={108}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate $m∠D$ using the fact that the interior angles of a triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠D+m∠BCD+m∠CBD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠D+m∠D+{108}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠D & ={72}^{∘} \\ m∠D & ={36}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
